mainTopic: Whether רבי שמעון requires ראשו ורובו to permit eating an animal born to a kosher mother, plus a question about donkey urine
overview: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון holds: if a cow gives birth to a camel-like animal that has some of its mother's features, may it be eaten, or must its head and most of its body (ראשו ורובו) look like the mother? A first ברייתא is brought, but it may speak only about בכורה. A second ברייתא allows an animal that 'comes with one sign.' It sounds like רבי שמעון, but the גמרא answers that this תנא agrees with him on only one point. This happens twice, the second time after רבי ירמיה explains how a kosher animal can become pregnant from a קלוט born to a cow. Along the way, the גמרא shows that the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is not about זה וזה גורם. Each one keeps his usual rule and reads the פסוק 'שה כשבים ושה עזים' as a special case. Finally, a ברייתא of רבי שמעון about 'גמל גמל' proves that he requires ראשו ורובו even for eating. The amud ends with a new question put to רב ששת about donkey urine, and his answer from the wording of the משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is a partial resemblance enough to permit eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking its question. A camel-like animal born to a cow that looks somewhat different from a camel: is it permitted to eat, or is it the same as a regular camel?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is different from a camel, maybe it is fine to eat. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its question about רבי שמעון's view. If the offspring is not a full camel but has some of its mother's features, is that enough to permit eating it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון forbids a camel born to a cow. The question is where the line falls. Side one says any change from a camel makes it permitted. Side two says there is no difference, so it would still need ראשו ורובו to look like the mother before it can be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different / it changed
it is fine; it is permitted
or perhaps
there is no difference

phrases.english: It is different from a camel
phrases.notes: He means the offspring of a cow that looks like a camel but also has some of its mother's features.

phrases.english: so it is fine (permitted to eat),
or perhaps there is no difference?
phrases.notes: In other words, maybe it is treated just like a regular camel unless its head and most of its body look like the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a question the גמרא began on the previous lines of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי שמעון, does a partial resemblance to the kosher mother permit eating, or is ראשו ורובו still required?

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show head and majority is needed for eating too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher kind is forbidden to eat, and if its head and majority look like the mother it is a בכור. The גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון requires ראשו ורובו for eating as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a kosher animal gave birth to a kind of non-kosher animal, it is forbidden to eat. If its head and most of its body look like its mother, it has the status of a בכור. We learn from this that רבי שמעון requires head and majority for eating too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a ברייתא that follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only one measure, ראשו ורובו, and does not mention a partial resemblance at all. The גמרא reads that measure as the line for the whole ברייתא, eating included. So a partial resemblance would not be enough, and the animal stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a kosher animal
a non-kosher animal
its head and the majority of its body
it has firstborn (בכור) status
learn from this

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A kosher animal that gave birth to
a kind of non-kosher animal —
it is forbidden to eat,
and if its head and most of its body resemble its mother —
it has the status of a firstborn.
Learn from this:
for eating, too, requires
Rabbi Shimon, its head and the majority of its body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי שמעון, ראשו ורובו is needed to permit eating, so a partial resemblance is not enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher kind.

steps.title: No, head and majority is only for firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא's ראשו ורובו may apply only to בכורה, not to eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. That requirement is only for firstborn status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'head and majority' sit in the בכורה clause of the ברייתא. So they may say nothing about eating. For eating, a partial resemblance might still be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: specifically; only

phrases.english: No, it is specifically for firstborn status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading ראשו ורובו as a condition for eating.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ראשו ורובו clause covers eating, but it may be limited to בכורה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording supports limiting it to firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the ברייתא's wording backs up the rejection. It stops talking about eating and turns to בכור, so ראשו ורובו belongs only to בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording shows this too. The ברייתא leaves eating behind and moves on to the firstborn. Learn from this that רבי שמעון requires head and majority for firstborn status, but not for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports step 3 from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא finishes its ruling on eating and only then brings up ראשו ורובו in a new clause about בכור. That switch suggests the measure belongs only to the בכור rule. If so, a partial resemblance could be enough for eating.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording also shows this (a support from careful reading)
he left it
he turned to; he took up

phrases.english: The wording shows this too,
since it leaves the topic of eating
and turns to the firstborn.
Learn from this:
it is for firstborn status that
Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body,
but for eating — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection in step 3 from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון requires ראשו ורובו only for בכורה, not for eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the ברייתא's clauses: the eating ruling comes first, then a separate clause about בכור.

steps.title: Head and majority may apply to eating too; firstborn needed saying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading from the wording. Maybe ראשו ורובו is needed for eating too. The ברייתא only had to say it about בכור because 'אך בכור שור' might suggest the whole animal must be an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that he requires it for eating too. It had to be said about the firstborn, because you might have thought: since it is written 'But the firstborn of an ox,' it must be an ox and its firstborn an ox, and head and majority would not be enough unless the whole animal looks like an ox. So the ברייתא teaches us that head and majority is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the support from the wording in step 4. It explains why the ברייתא mentions ראשו ורובו by בכור even if the same rule applies to eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The switch to בכור does not prove eating is different. The ברייתא had a special reason to speak about בכור: the פסוק 'אך בכור שור' might suggest the whole animal must look like an ox. The ברייתא teaches that ראשו ורובו is enough even there. So eating could still require ראשו ורובו, and this ברייתא cannot settle the question. The גמרא settles it later, in Steps 24-25.

keyTerms.meaning: really, I can tell you (keeping the original view)
it was needed (to be said)
you might have thought
'But the firstborn of an ox' (במדבר יח:יז)
it teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. The worry with בכור was that ראשו ורובו might be too little, because the whole animal would need to look like an ox. The question about eating is whether something less than ראשו ורובו is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that ראשו ורובו is enough for בכורה. It does not settle whether a partial resemblance to the mother permits eating according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you:
for eating, too, he requires it,
phrases.notes: Meaning רבי שמעון requires head and majority to look like the mother before it is permitted to eat.

phrases.english: and the firstborn case needed to be stated,
because you might have thought:
since it is written, "But the firstborn of an ox,"

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר,
phrases.english: it does not count unless the mother is an ox and its firstborn is an ox,
and its head and majority would not be enough for it
unless the whole animal looks like an ox,
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is teaching that head and majority is enough for firstborn status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support from the wording in step 4 and restores the possibility raised in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the switch to בכור proves eating needs only a partial resemblance.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The switch to בכור can be explained another way: the פסוק 'אך בכור שור' might have suggested that the whole animal must look like an ox, so the ברייתא had to teach that ראשו ורובו is enough for בכורה.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: 'this' you may not eat, but one with a single sign you may
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from the פסוק 'אך את זה לא תאכלו' that some animals born to kosher mothers are forbidden, but one that comes 'with one sign' is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'But this you shall not eat from those that chew the cud and from those that split the hoof.' 'This' you may not eat, but you may eat one that comes with one sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the question from Step 1 by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source; the ברייתא keeps explaining itself in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'זה' in the פסוק as a limit. 'This' kind is forbidden, but there is another kind, one that 'comes with one sign', that the תורה allows. Our question is about a strange-looking animal born to a cow, so the גמרא hopes this ברייתא tells us when such an animal may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that chew the cud.
Animals that have split hooves.
An animal that comes with one sign, meaning it has one feature of its mother.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"But this you shall not eat
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא (11:4) that lists the camel and similar animals as forbidden.

phrases.english: from those that chew the cud and from those that split the hoof",
'this' you may not eat,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד.
phrases.english: but you may eat one that comes with one sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַךְ אֶת זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 5, the גמרא tries a new ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The question from Step 1: may a camel-like animal born to a cow be eaten?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the word 'זה' in ויקרא 11:4.

steps.title: Which animal is the one that comes with one sign?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what kind of animal it means by 'one that comes with one sign.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And which animal is this one that comes with one sign?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to ask for a definition of the new phrase it just used. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Comes with one sign' is unclear. The ברייתא wants to pin down exactly which case the Torah allows, so it asks before giving the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And which one? A question asking for a definition.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי זֶה זֶה הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד?
phrases.english: And which is this one that comes with one sign?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי זֶה זֶה הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is meant by 'הבא בסימן אחד'?

steps.title: A non-kosher-looking baby born to a kosher mother from a kosher father
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers: it is a טמא-looking animal born to a kosher mother, where the father was also kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a non-kosher animal born from a kosher animal, and its father was also kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The permitted animal looks טמא, but both of its parents are טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby looks like a non-kosher animal, yet it is allowed because it came from a kosher mother and a kosher father. This is the first opinion, and it requires both parents to be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-kosher (here: looks like a non-kosher kind).
Kosher.
Its conception. This means the father that made the mother pregnant.

phrases.english: This is a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one,
and its conception is from a kosher one.
phrases.notes: 'Its conception' means the father. So both the mother and the father are kosher animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טמא-looking animal born from a kosher mother whose father was also kosher.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the father and mother must both be sheep
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether a non-kosher father would also be allowed, and says no. From 'שה כשבים ושה עזים' it learns that the father and the mother must both be sheep. This is רבי יהושע's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be that it is allowed even if the father was non-kosher? The verse says 'שה כשבים ושה עזים'. It is not allowed until its father is a ram and its mother is a ewe. These are the words of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea, that even a non-kosher father would be fine, and then rejects it with a פסוק. It names this opinion as רבי יהושע's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כשבים is plural, so רבי יהושע reads it as 'a lamb from sheep,' meaning two sheep: a father and a mother. A kosher mother alone is not enough. Both parents must be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought. It raises an idea that will be rejected.
The verse comes to teach. This brings a פסוק to settle the question.
A lamb of sheep and a kid of goats (from the list of kosher animals in דברים 14:4).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parents. 'Born from' refers to the mother, and 'its conception' (עיבורו) refers to the father. The argument here is only about the father.

phrases.english: Could it be even if its conception is from a non-kosher one?
The verse teaches: "a lamb of sheep and a kid of goats,"
phrases.notes: This is from the list of kosher animals in דברים 14:4. 'Sheep' is plural, so he reads it as two sheep.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אָבִיו כֶּבֶשׂ וְאִמּוֹ כִּבְשָׂה,
phrases.english: not until its father is a ram and its mother is a ewe,
these are the words of רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why Step 8 needed a kosher father, and gives the source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: a טמא-looking offspring is allowed only if both its father and mother are kosher.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the פסוק adds a case with a non-kosher father
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues. The פסוק would not come to permit something already permitted. It must add a new case: a טמא-looking animal born from a kosher mother even if the father was non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: The verse did not come to permit what is already permitted. It came to add to what is permitted. And which case is this? A non-kosher animal born from a kosher mother, where its father was non-kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי יהושע. He says the פסוק must be teaching something new, so it permits even when the father was not kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: an animal from two kosher parents is obviously allowed anyway, so the תורה would not need a special teaching for it. The extra teaching must cover a harder case, a kosher mother with a non-kosher father.

keyTerms.meaning: To permit what is already permitted.
To add a new case to what is permitted.
The verse.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב לְהַתִּיר אֶת הַמּוּתָּר,
phrases.english: The verse did not come to permit what is already permitted,
but rather to add to what is permitted,
and which case is this?
A non-kosher animal born from a kosher one
and its conception is from a non-kosher one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב לְהַתִּיר אֶת הַמּוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהושע in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a טמא-looking offspring of a kosher mother is allowed even if the father was non-kosher.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: 'שור שה כשבים ושה עזים' in any case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks whether the teaching might apply only to a kosher father. He answers from the פסוק 'שור שה כשבים ושה עזים' that it applies in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it applies only when its father was kosher? The verse teaches: 'an ox, a lamb of sheep and a kid of goats.' It is allowed in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר raises the opposite possibility and rejects it with the פסוק. He concludes that the animal is allowed no matter what the father was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the same פסוק that רבי יהושע used, but he draws the opposite conclusion: 'in any case,' even if only the mother was kosher. This finishes the ברייתא. The גמרא has not yet explained how this answers the question from Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only. It raises another possibility to reject.
In any case, no matter what.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע requires both parents to be kosher. רבי אליעזר allows the animal once the mother is kosher, even if the father was not. Both agree that a 'one sign' animal born to a kosher mother can be permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּהוֹר?
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only when its conception is from a kosher one?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שׁוֹר שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְשֵׂה עִזִּים״
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "an ox, a lamb of sheep and a kid of goats"
in any case.
phrases.notes: Meaning it's allowed even if only the mother was a kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי אליעזר's view in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a non-kosher father does not matter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 14:4, 'שור שה כשבים ושה עזים', read as 'in any case.'

steps.title: A proof about רבי שמעון from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא calls the animal born to a kosher mother 'טמא', like רבי שמעון, yet allows eating one that has one sign. So רבי שמעון does not need the head and most of the body to look like the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The author of the ברייתא calls this animal 'טמא', just like רבי שמעון does, and still says: but you may eat one that comes with one sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא from the earlier steps to try to prove what רבי שמעון holds. Since the ברייתא sounds like רבי שמעון, its rule about 'one sign' should be his rule too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון forbids a camel-looking animal born to a cow, and the ברייתא also calls such an animal 'טמא'. Since the same ברייתא allows an animal with just one sign of its mother, the גמרא argues that רבי שמעון also needs only one sign, not the head and most of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: He calls it
Non-kosher
A sign or feature (here, a feature like its mother's)

phrases.english: He calls it "non-kosher",
phrases.notes: 'He' is the author of the ברייתא from the last few steps.

phrases.english: like רבי שמעון,
and he says: but you may eat
one that comes with one sign!
phrases.notes: This means one feature that looks like its mother. The exclamation shows this is meant as a proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי לֵיהּ טָמֵא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in steps 6-11 as evidence for רבי שמעון's view, to answer the question from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון allows eating the animal when it has only one sign like its mother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, which calls the animal 'טמא' like רבי שמעון but allows 'הבא בסימן אחד'.

steps.title: The ברייתא agrees with רבי שמעון on only one point
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא's author agrees with רבי שמעון on one point and disagrees with him on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with him on one thing and argues with him on one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 12. Just because the ברייתא sounds like רבי שמעון on one point does not mean it follows him on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רבי שמעון that a טמא-looking animal born to a kosher mother is forbidden. On the 'one sign' rule it may disagree, so רבי שמעון could still require the head and most of the body to look like the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: The author of a ברייתא or משנה
He holds like him
In one thing
He argues with him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that a ברייתא follows a תנא on every point just because it matches him on one point. A ברייתא can agree with him on one law and argue with him on the next.

phrases.english: This tanna holds
like him in one thing,
phrases.notes: The one thing is that this animal is called 'טמא' and is forbidden.

phrases.english: and argues with him in one thing.
phrases.notes: The other thing is the 'one sign' rule, where רבי שמעון may be stricter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected entirely. The ברייתא cannot show what רבי שמעון holds about 'one sign'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון on everything, but it may agree with him on only one point.

steps.title: Can a kosher animal become pregnant from a non-kosher one?
steps.stepSummary: Some raise a challenge to the ברייתא's case: a kosher mother made pregnant by a non-kosher father. Can that even happen?
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who challenge and then answer: its pregnancy came from a non-kosher animal — can she really become pregnant that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the discussion, where some people attack the ברייתא's case itself. They ask whether a kosher mother can become pregnant from a non-kosher father at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי אליעזר's view in the ברייתא spoke of a kosher mother whose father was non-kosher. This challenge says that case may be impossible in nature, which would make the ברייתא's teaching pointless. The words 'ומותיב' tell us an answer will follow later.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who raise a difficulty and resolve it
Pregnancy
Can she become pregnant?

phrases.english: And there are those who raise a difficulty and resolve it:
its pregnancy is from a non-kosher animal
can she become pregnant?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a different version of the discussion. Instead of a proof about רבי שמעון, it opens by challenging the ברייתא's case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's case of a kosher mother made pregnant by a non-kosher father (step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that kind of pregnancy is impossible, the ברייתא is describing a case that cannot happen.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: different kinds of animals cannot breed together
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is backed by רבי יהושע בן לוי. He says an animal never becomes pregnant from a different type: kosher and non-kosher, large and small, or domestic and wild.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say: a non-kosher animal never becomes pregnant from a kosher one, nor a kosher one from a non-kosher one, nor a large one from a small one, nor a small one from a large one, nor a domestic animal from a wild animal, nor a wild animal from a domestic animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the challenge from step 14. רבי יהושע בן לוי says outright that a kosher mother cannot become pregnant from a non-kosher father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי lists three pairs of mismatched animals that cannot breed together, in both directions. The second item, 'a kosher one from a non-kosher one', is exactly the ברייתא's case, so the ברייתא seems to describe something impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: A large animal (such as a cow)
A small animal (such as a sheep or goat)
A domestic animal
A wild animal

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement teaches the basic rule that animals of different types do not breed together. The גמרא will need to answer it to keep the ברייתא's case.

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say:
An animal never becomes pregnant
not a non-kosher one from a kosher one,
nor a kosher one from a non-kosher one,
nor a large one from a small one,
nor a small one from a large one,
nor a domestic animal from a wild animal,
nor a wild animal from a domestic animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: A kosher animal cannot become pregnant from a non-kosher one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: The one exception to the rule about mixed pregnancies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי ends his statement with one exception. רבי אליעזר and the חכמים who argue with him held that a חיה can become pregnant from a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for רבי אליעזר and the ones who argued with him, who said that a wild animal can become pregnant from a domestic animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, who backs up the challenge from step 14. His one exception does not help the ברייתא's case, so the challenge still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule is that different types of animals never make each other pregnant. The only people who allowed any exception spoke about a חיה and a בהמה, not about a kosher and a non-kosher animal. So the ברייתא's case of a kosher mother and a non-kosher father still looks impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, such as a deer or gazelle
A domestic animal, such as a goat or cow
Becomes pregnant
Literally 'his dispute'; here it means the people who argued with him

phrases.english: except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants,
phrases.notes: This is still רבי יהושע בן לוי talking. 'His disputants' means the חכמים who argued with רבי אליעזר about this case.

phrases.english: who would say
a wild animal can become pregnant from a domestic animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote from רבי יהושע בן לוי that began in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge from step 14 that a kosher mother cannot become pregnant from a non-kosher father
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule and its one exception

steps.title: The father was a closed-hoof animal born to a cow
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that the ברייתא's non-kosher father was a קלוט whose own mother was a cow. That is why the pregnancy is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה said: the case is where the mother became pregnant from a closed-hoofed animal that was born to a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge from step 14. He shows that the ברייתא's case can really happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קלוט has hooves that are not split, so it counts as non-kosher. But this one was born from a cow, so it is really the same kind of animal as a cow. Because of that, a cow can become pregnant from it, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with closed hooves that are not split
Became pregnant
The offspring of a cow

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said:
where it became pregnant from a closed-hoofed animal that was the offspring of a cow,
phrases.notes: The father looks non-kosher because its hooves are closed. But its mother was a cow, so it is really a cow's kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּאִיעַבַּר מִקָּלוּט בֶּן פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 14 and backed up in steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The non-kosher father was a completely different kind of animal, so the pregnancy could never happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father was a קלוט born to a cow, so it is the same kind as the mother, and the pregnancy can happen.

steps.title: The proof about רבי שמעון comes back
steps.stepSummary: Now that the case is shown to be possible, the גמרא repeats its earlier proof. The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, yet it allows eating an animal that has one sign of its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא is said according to רבי שמעון, and it says: but you may eat one that comes with one sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge about the case is answered, so the גמרא goes back to the proof from step 12 and says it again. The question is whether רבי שמעון allows an animal with only one sign of its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the ברייתא calls the קלוט father 'טמא' even though it was born to a cow, and only רבי שמעון treats such an animal as non-kosher. So the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. Yet it also allows eating an offspring with just one sign of its mother. That suggests רבי שמעון would not need the head and most of the body to look like the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
A sign or feature, here one that is like the mother's

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new proof. The גמרא is saying again the proof from step 12, because the side question about whether the case can happen has now been answered.

phrases.english: and he says it according to Rabbi Shimon,
and he says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד!
phrases.english: but you may eat that which comes with one characteristic!
phrases.notes: This means an animal that has just one feature like its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר, וְקָאָמַר: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that step 17 has answered the challenge, the גמרא returns to the proof from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not need the head and most of the body to look like the mother
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, which follows רבי שמעון but allows eating an animal with one sign

steps.title: The ברייתא agrees with רבי שמעון on only one point
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away again. The author of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון about calling the offspring טמא, but argues with him about the one sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with him on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the rejection from step 13. The ברייתא does not follow רבי שמעון on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רבי שמעון that a non-kosher animal born to a kosher mother is forbidden. It argues with him about an animal with one sign: the ברייתא allows it, but רבי שמעון still needs the head and most of the body to look like the mother. So nothing can be proven about רבי שמעון from the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the time of the משנה; here, the author of the ברייתא
On one point
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא matches רבי שמעון only about calling such an animal טמא. So it cannot prove that רבי שמעון allows eating with just one sign. The answer comes in Steps 24-25.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This tanna holds like him on one point,
phrases.notes: The one point he agrees on is that a non-kosher animal born to a kosher mother is forbidden.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on one point.
phrases.notes: The point he disagrees on is the animal with one sign. The ברייתא allows it, but רבי שמעון does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof that step 18 just repeated.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof about what רבי שמעון holds
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון on everything, but it only agrees with him on one point.

steps.title: Is the argument really about זה וזה גורם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question. Does רבי אליעזר hold that זה וזה גורם is מותר, and רבי יהושע that it is אסור?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי אליעזר holds that when two things together cause something, it is permitted, and רבי יהושע holds that when two things together cause something, it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in the ברייתא. It asks whether their argument depends on the rule of זה וזה גורם, and this question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a kosher mother and a non-kosher father together produce the offspring. רבי אליעזר allows eating it, so perhaps he holds that when a permitted thing and a forbidden thing cause something together, the result is מותר. רבי יהושע forbids it, so perhaps he holds the result is אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is this to say...?' The גמרא is testing whether something follows
When two things, one permitted and one forbidden, together cause a result
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: זה וזה גורם is a general rule that comes up in many places in ש״ס. This question asks whether this argument depends on that rule or on something else.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Eliezer holds:
when this and that cause it, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' are the kosher mother and the non-kosher father, which together produce the baby animal.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
when this and that cause it, it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and starts a new question about the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע depends on the rule of זה וזה גורם

steps.title: The two רבנן seem to hold the opposite views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 20. In the case of the offspring of a טריפה, רבי אליעזר forbids it and רבי יהושע permits it, which is the opposite of what was just suggested.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have heard them say the opposite! About the offspring of a טריפה, רבי אליעזר says it may not be brought on the מזבח, and רבי יהושע says it may be brought on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from Step 20 by pointing to another place where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה mother with a kosher father is also a case of זה וזה גורם, because two parents together make the baby. There רבי אליעזר forbids and רבי יהושע permits. So it looks like רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם is אסור and רבי יהושע holds it is מותר, which is the reverse of Step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite
The offspring of an animal that is a טריפה (has a fatal defect)
Onto the altar, meaning brought as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In Step 20 the question was about a kosher animal pregnant from a non-kosher one. Here the case is a טריפה mother. The גמרא compares them because both are cases of זה וזה גורם.

phrases.english: But we have heard them say the opposite:
The offspring of a טריפה:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It may not be offered on the altar,
And Rabbi Yehoshua says:
It may be offered on the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion raised in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם is מותר and רבי יהושע holds it is אסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of the offspring of a טריפה, also a case of two causes, רבי אליעזר forbids and רבי יהושע permits. That shows the reverse positions.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: usually forbidden, but the פסוק permits here
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does hold that זה וזה גורם is אסור. But for a kosher mother animal, the extra word שה in the פסוק teaches that the baby is permitted anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: In general, רבי אליעזר holds that when two causes work together, it is forbidden. But here is different. If the baby were forbidden, the תורה could have written 'שה כשבים ועזים.' Why does it say 'שה' and then 'ושה' again? Learn from it: a שה is permitted in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for רבי אליעזר. He keeps his usual rule, but a special פסוק makes this case different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually רבי אליעזר forbids זה וזה גורם, which fits the טריפה case. But the פסוק repeats the word שה ('שה כשבים ושה עזים'), and an extra word teaches something. It teaches that the animal counts as a שה in any case, even if only its mother is a kosher sheep or goat.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, in other cases
When two causes together produce the result (here, two parents)
Here it is different
A שה in any case, even if only one parent is a kosher sheep or goat

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a רבי keeps his general rule, and a special פסוק explains why one case comes out differently.

phrases.english: In general, Rabbi Eliezer holds:
When both this and that cause the result, it is forbidden,
But here it is different,
For if so, let the verse write:
"A seh of sheep and goats,"
phrases.notes: This is a shorter version of the פסוק in דברים about which animals you may eat.

phrases.english: Why do I need "seh" and then "and seh" again?
Learn from it:
A seh is permitted in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 for רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule stays the same; a special פסוק creates an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אליעזר permits a baby from a non-kosher father, we might think he holds זה וזה גורם is מותר, which clashes with the טריפה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds זה וזה גורם is אסור, but the extra שה permits the baby of a kosher mother animal.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: usually permitted, but the פסוק forbids here
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע does hold that זה וזה גורם is מותר. But the plural words כשבים ועזים teach that both parents must be sheep for the baby to be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע could say to you: in general, when two causes work together, it is permitted. But here, if so, the תורה could have written 'שור כשב ועז.' Why do I need the plural 'כשבים ועזים'? Learn from it that the baby is permitted only if its father is a sheep and its mother is a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the challenge for רבי יהושע in the same way. He keeps his usual rule, but a פסוק changes this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually רבי יהושע permits זה וזה גורם, which fits the טריפה case. But the פסוק uses the plural כשבים ועזים, when a simple singular would have been enough. The plural hints at two parents, so the baby is permitted only when both its father and mother are that kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you, a way to show how a רבי would defend his view
Sheep and goats, in the plural
Its father is a male sheep and its mother a female sheep

steps.whatToRemember: Each רבי keeps his general view on זה וזה גורם (רבי אליעזר: אסור, רבי יהושע: מותר). For animals born of mixed parents, each one reads a special פסוק that gives the reverse result.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua could say to you:
In general, when both this and that cause the result, it is permitted,
But here, if so, let the verse write:
"Ox, sheep and goat,"
Why do I need "sheep and goats" in the plural?
Learn from it: it is not permitted unless
Its father is a male sheep and its mother is a female sheep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching answer for רבי יהושע, finishing the reply to Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule stays the same; a special פסוק creates an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהושע forbids a baby from a non-kosher father, we might think he holds זה וזה גורם is אסור, which clashes with the טריפה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds זה וזה גורם is מותר, but the plural כשבים ועזים requires both parents to be kosher sheep or goats.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון about a camel born from a cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the open question about רבי שמעון. It brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון says a camel born from a cow is forbidden, but if its head and most of its body look like its mother, it may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says, 'גמל' is written two times. One teaches a camel born from a camel, and the other teaches a camel born from a cow. And if its head and most of its body look like its mother, it is permitted to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: With תא שמע, the גמרא returns to the earlier question about what רבי שמעון holds, and brings a new source to try to settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גמל appears twice in the תורה, once in ויקרא and once in דברים. רבי שמעון learns from this that even a camel-looking baby born from a cow is forbidden. But he adds that if its head and most of its body look like the kosher mother, it may be eaten. The גמרא brings this to learn how much the baby must look like its mother before רבי שמעון permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: A camel born from a cow
Its head and most of its body
Permitted to be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits every camel born from a cow. He forbids it, unless its head and most of its body look like the cow.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Shimon says:
"Camel," "camel": it is written two times,
phrases.notes: The camel is listed as non-kosher both in ויקרא and in דברים, so the second time must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: Both a camel born from a camel,
And a camel born from a cow are forbidden,
And if its head and most of its body look like its mother,
It is permitted to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע discussion and returns to the question about רבי שמעון from Step 1, after the earlier proofs (Steps 2-5, 12-19) were rejected.
steps.raayaObject: What רבי שמעון holds about the baby of a kosher animal that looks like a non-kosher animal but has some features of its mother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון learns from the double word גמל and permits the baby only if its head and most of its body look like its mother.

steps.title: רבי שמעון needs head and most of the body even for eating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from Step 24 proves that רבי שמעון requires the head and most of the body to look like the mother even for permission to eat the animal. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: even for eating, רבי שמעון requires the head and the majority of the body to resemble the mother. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 24 and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open question was whether רבי שמעון's demand for 'head and most of the body' applies only to the laws of a firstborn or also to eating. The ברייתא speaks about eating, so his demand applies there too. A partial resemblance is not enough to permit the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; a conclusion is being drawn
For eating
Its head and most of its body

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, an animal born from a kosher mother may be eaten only if its head and most of its body look like hers. This applies to eating, not just to firstborn laws.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
for eating as well, Rabbi Shimon requires
its head and the majority of its body (to resemble the mother).
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws and confirms the conclusion of the ברייתא brought in Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון requires head and most of the body to resemble the mother even to permit eating.

steps.title: Is donkey urine forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about what comes out of a non-kosher animal. It records a question asked of רב ששת: what is the law of a donkey's urine?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'because what comes out of the non-kosher animal and so on.' They asked רב ששת: what is the law of donkey urine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and opens a new question about donkey urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that products of a non-kosher animal, like donkey milk, are forbidden. The question is whether urine also counts as something that 'comes out' of the forbidden animal.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes out of a non-kosher animal
They asked him
Urine
Donkey

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'Because what comes out of the non-kosher animal, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The rest of that line is: 'is non-kosher, and what comes out of the kosher animal is kosher.'

phrases.english: They asked of Rav Sheshet:
The urine of a donkey, what is its law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether donkey urine is forbidden as a product of a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: Why ask only about donkeys?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the question was limited to donkeys. Why not ask about the urine of horses and camels too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not ask the question about horses and camels as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the scope of the question. Horses and camels are also non-kosher, so why single out the donkey?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If urine is a possible problem, it would seem to be a problem for every non-kosher animal. Asking only about donkeys suggests there is something special about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him ask (about this too)
Horses and camels

phrases.english: And let them ask also about that of horses and camels?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the question in Step 26 is limited to donkeys.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrow scope of the question in Step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Horses and camels are also non-kosher, so the same question should apply to them.

steps.title: Horse and camel urine is just water
steps.stepSummary: There was no question about horses and camels. Their urine is clear and does not look like milk, so it is simply water passing through the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: About horses and camels there was no question, because their urine is not cloudy and does not look like milk. Water goes in and water comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why horses and camels were left out: their urine is obviously permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clear urine shows that nothing of the animal's body is mixed in. It is just the water the animal drank. So it is not a 'product' of the non-kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Cloudy, murky
Water went in, water came out

phrases.english: About that of horses and camels they did not ask,
because it is not cloudy and does not resemble milk;
water went in, water came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 by explaining why horses and camels are not in doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All non-kosher animals' urine should be in question.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clear urine is just water, so only cloudy donkey urine is in question.

steps.title: The two sides of the donkey question
steps.stepSummary: Donkey urine is cloudy and looks like milk. Maybe it is drawn out of the body and is forbidden. Or maybe it is still just water, and the cloudiness comes only from the heat of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question was about the donkey, whose urine is cloudy and looks like milk. What is the law? Is it drawn from its body, and so forbidden? Or perhaps water goes in and water comes out, and the cloudiness is just from the heat of the flesh?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the donkey question again in a sharper form and lays out both possible sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side treats cloudy urine like milk: something drawn out of the animal's body, and therefore forbidden. The second side says it is still only water, and the body's heat just made it cloudy. The question is waiting for רב ששת's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawn out, sucked out (from the body)
The heat of the flesh
Or perhaps

phrases.english: When they asked, it was about that of a donkey,
which is cloudy and resembles milk. What is the law?
Is it drawn out from its body, and so it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא מַיָּא עוּל מַיָּא נְפוּק,
phrases.english: or perhaps water went in, water came out,
and the fact that it is cloudy comes from the heat of the flesh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting horses and camels aside, it states the donkey question from Step 26 more precisely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether donkey urine is a bodily product (forbidden) or just water colored by body heat (permitted).

steps.title: רב ששת answers from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the answer is already in the משנה. He points out that the משנה says 'מִן הַטָּמֵא' rather than 'מִטָּמֵא', and begins to draw a lesson from that wording. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You learned it in the משנה: 'What comes out of the non-kosher animal is non-kosher, and what comes out of the kosher animal is kosher.' It does not say 'from a non-kosher animal' (מִטָּמֵא); rather it says 'from...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins answering the donkey-urine question by looking closely at one small word in the משנה. The answer is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת notices the משנה wrote 'מִן הַטָּמֵא' instead of the shorter 'מִטָּמֵא'. He is setting up a lesson from this difference in wording. The full explanation and the ruling come in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in the משנה)
From a non-kosher animal (the shorter wording)
It does not say

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of רב ששת's sentence. Do not try to guess his ruling yet. It comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
'Because what comes out of the non-kosher animal is non-kosher,'
'and what comes out of the kosher animal is kosher.'
It does not say 'from a non-kosher animal' (מִטָּמֵא),
but rather 'from...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question laid out in Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is drawn from the משנה's choice of 'מִן הַטָּמֵא' over 'מִטָּמֵא'. The conclusion continues on the next amud.
